paper_title: Laboratory Constraints on the Neutron-Spin Coupling of feV-scale Axions
coupling_convention: g_aNN 95% upper limit in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 5 (derivative axion-neutron coupling, NOT converted to dimensionless g_an)
notes: Re-analysis of ~40 days of Princeton K-3He co-magnetometer data (originally a long-range force search) using a stochastic-field frequency-domain likelihood. Median 95% CL upper limit g_aNN < 2.4e-10 GeV^-1 for axion masses 0.4-4 feV (4e-16 to 4e-15 eV), encoded here as a flat two-point band. Full analysis spans 0.01-10 Hz (~4e-17 to 4.1e-14 eV) with limits degrading toward the edges; the point at 4.1e-14 eV (~10 Hz, 41 feV) is inferred from the text statement that the limit is ~2 orders of magnitude stronger than NASDUCK's 1e-6 GeV^-1 there, so it is approximate. Values emitted are raw g_aNN in GeV^-1 as reported by the paper (NOT converted to dimensionless g_an; conversion would require multiplying by 2*m_n). Paper assumes axions constitute all local DM but the numerical rho_DM value is not stated in the provided content (likely standard SHM value).
